what: Sanofi is a French pharmaceutical company. Its largest product by far is Dupixent, a medicine for eczema, asthma and related inflammatory diseases, and it is also one of the world's largest vaccine makers.
customers: Health systems, insurers and governments; vaccines are often bought under national programmes.
money: Dupixent and other immunology, rare disease and oncology medicines
flu, meningitis, polio and travel vaccines
older established products including diabetes treatments
moat: Dupixent's position in several large inflammatory diseases, vaccine manufacturing that takes years to build and license, and global regulatory reach.
risks: Dupixent dominates growth, so any setback matters disproportionately
It shares Dupixent economics with Regeneron
Several late-stage trials have disappointed in recent years
US and European price controls keep pressure on margins
opportunities: Dupixent keeps adding approved uses, each opening a new patient group
A heavy pipeline in immunology could produce the next growth driver
Separating its consumer health business leaves a more focused company
watch: Dupixent sales growth and the results of its late-stage immunology trials.
